comment: The core attributes focus mainly at access, dashboards and dissemination. DHIS2/HISP evidence treats information use as a decentralised cycle linking data quality, interpretation, feedback, action and renewed demand. Platform features specifically desgined to support data use include user-specific dashboards, maps, interpretations/discussion, internal messages, alerts and action tracking. These features enrich decision-point convenings such as data review meetings, healthworker supervision and policy dialogues. In essence, HMIS should promote translation of data into information, and track actions taken by HMIS actors.  Evidence: https://docs.dhis2.org/en/implement/health/chis-community-health-information-system/implementation/data-quality-and-use.html

These features enrich decision-point convenings such as data review meetings, healthworker supervision and policy dialogues. public.suggestedRevision: Add ‘decentralised information-to-action and feedback’ as a core capability. Require role-appropriate analytics at facility, district and national levels; interpretation/discussion; configurable alerts; action plans with owners and deadlines; follow-up and closure; supervisory feedback to data producers; and measurement of whether information changed decisions or services.
